narrative.overview: Tixora books tickets the way a travel site books flights: a trusted blue chrome carries browsing, wayfinding, and navigation, and a single green action color is spent only on the money moment — prices, availability, and every buy button. This replaced an earlier "vintage theater marquee" identity; that world is gone from the code entirely, and this document describes only what shipped. The chosen reference is Traveloka's booking-commerce visual language, not a ticketing-site or entertainment-brand default: deep-to-mid blue gradient hero bands, a white floating search/category panel overlapping the hero's lower edge, and white rounded cards resting on a soft blue-gray page ground. The system is calm and legible rather than theatrical. White and pale blue-gray surfaces dominate nearly every screen; blue and green are spent narrowly, on chrome and on action, not spread across whole page regions. The one deliberate exception is full-bleed blue: hero bands and the footer are fully blue, everything else is white-on-pale-ground. A single sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, carries both display and body type at a confident, tight-tracked scale — there is no separate display face.
keyCharacteristics: Deep-to-mid blue (#0c2c61 → #1966d6) owns navigation, hero bands, and wayfinding; green (#12a150) owns prices, availability, and every buy action — the two never trade roles.
A floating white panel overlapping a blue hero band's lower edge is the system's signature travel-booking motif.
White rounded-2xl cards float on a pale blue-gray ground with a soft ambient shadow, never a hard edge.
One typeface (Plus Jakarta Sans) for everything; hierarchy comes from weight, size, and tracking, not from a second family.
A boarding-pass-style e-ticket (dashed tear line with punched notches) closes the purchase loop.

rules.name: The Green-Is-Money Rule
rules.body: Green appears only where currency or availability changes hands or is at stake: prices, "X left" counts, and buy/pay CTAs. It never appears as brand decoration.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed-Blue Exception Rule
rules.body: Solid full-region blue is reserved for exactly two contexts — hero bands and the footer. Everywhere else, blue is a chrome accent on a white or pale surface, never a filled content region.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every weight of hierarchy — hero display down to a 12px badge — is Plus Jakarta Sans. No second (serif, mono, or system-display) face is introduced anywhere in the shipped screens.

rules.name: The Ambient-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always soft, diffuse, and large-radius (never a hard 1–2px offset). Depth communicates "resting on a surface," not a cutout or sticker.

dos: Do spend green exclusively on prices, availability, and buy/confirm actions (the Green-Is-Money Rule).
Do use the floating-panel-over-hero motif only for the primary browsing entry point (events list); it is a page-opening device, not a general card style.
Do keep all type in Plus Jakarta Sans; build hierarchy with weight/size/tracking, not a second family.
Do use soft ambient shadows (card-shadow/card-shadow-lg/floating-panel) for all elevation; never a hard 1–2px offset shadow.
donts: Don't fill a content region solid blue outside the hero band and footer — blue elsewhere is chrome and accent only.
Don't introduce a second typeface for "display" moments; the system deliberately has none.
Don't use amber or red for anything beyond their confirmed roles (urgency/pending, destructive/error/cancelled respectively) — they are not general accent colors.
Don't give cards a hard border in place of a shadow; the line hairline is for internal dividers only, not card silhouettes.
